source.title: On some open problems in reliability theory

accepted.question_text: For the reliability model of an unreliable machine with state densities p0(x,t) and p1(x,t) satisfying the PDE system ∂p0/∂t + ∂p0/∂x = -(λ(x)+μ(x))p0, ∂p1/∂t + ∂p1/∂x = -η(x)p1, boundary conditions p0(0,t)=δ(t)+∫_0^∞ p1(x,t)η(x)dx and p1(0,t)=∫_0^∞ p0(x,t)λ(x)dx, and initial data p0(x,0)=δ(x), p1(x,0)=0, determine an efficient method for inverting the Laplace-transform formulas (3.13) and (3.14) in the general nonconstant-rate case λ(x), μ(x), η(x), so that one obtains the explicit time-dependent solution of the system.
accepted.context_brief: Inverse Laplace transform for the base unreliable-machine model

evidence.quote: In general case, we determine the Laplace transform of the time-dependent solution of the model, but we could not obtain the Laplace inverse transform and therefore we leave it as an open problem.

Remark 1. If we can determine the Laplace inverse transform of (3.13) and (3.14), then we can get the time-dependent solution of the equation system (1.1)∼(1.5). But, until today we have not discovered an efficient method to resolve this problem.

accepted.question_text: Consider Linton's 1976 two-unit parallel redundant system with state variables q0,i(x,t), q1,i(x,t), and q2,j(x,t), where q0,i tracks states with no failed units and unit 2 in the i-th failure stage, q1,i tracks states where unit 1 is down and unit 2 is in the i-th failure stage, q2,j tracks states where unit 2 is down and in the j-th repair phase, λ>0 and μ>0 are unit parameters, g(x) is the repair rate of unit 1, and f(x) is the failure rate of unit 2. In the nonconstant-rate case for g(x) and f(x), determine whether this PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.

evidence.quote: Where (x, t) ∈ [0, ∞) × [0, ∞); p0,i(x, t) (1 ≤ i ≤ k) is the probability that at moment t, no units are down, unit 2 is in the ith stage of failure, and unit 1 has been operating for an amount of time x; p1,i(x, t) (1 ≤ i ≤ k) is the probability that at moment t, unit 1 is down, unit 2 is in the ith stage of failure and an amount of x, has already been spent on the current repair of unit 1; p2,j(x, t) (1 ≤ j ≤ m) are the probability that at moment t, unit 2 is down, unit 2 is in the jth phase of repair, and unit 1 has been operating for an amount of time x; λ > 0 and µ > 0 are parameters of unit 1 and unit 2 respectively; g(x) is the repair rate of unit 1; f(x) is the failure rate of unit 2, δ(·) is the Dirac-delta function.
When g(x) and f(x) are non-constants, well-posedness of the above model and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until today.

accepted.question_text: For the 1993 Li-Shi two-unit parallel system with preemptive priority, whose state variables p0,i(x,t), p1,i(x,t), p2(x,u,t), p3(x,t), and p4(x,u,t) describe the operating, repair, waiting-for-repair, and suspended-repair configurations of the two units, with a1>0 an Erlang parameter, a2(x) the repair rate of unit 1, b1(x) the life rate, and b2(x) the repair rate of unit 2, determine whether the full PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.
accepted.context_brief: Li et al. preemptive-priority two-unit system

evidence.quote: Where (x, u, t) ∈ [0, ∞) × [0, ∞) × [0, ∞); p0,i(x, t) is the probability that at time t two units are operating and the operating unit 1 is in phase i, and the age of unit 2 is x, i = 1, 2, · · · , m; p1,i(x, t) is the probability that at time t unit 1 is operating, the operating phase is i and unit 2 is being repaired and the elapsed time of the failed unit 2 is x, i = 1, 2, · · · , m; p2(x, u, t) is the probability that at time t unit 2 is operating and unit 1 is being repaired, the elapsed repair time of the failed unit 1 is x, and the age of unit 2 is u, ; p3(x, t) is the probability that at time t unit 1 is being repaired and unit 2 is waiting for repair, and the elapsed repair time of the failed unit 1 is x; p4(x, u, t) is the probability that at time t unit 1 is being repaired and unit 2 is in "suspended repair", and the elapsed repair time of the failed unit 1 is x and the elapsed time of the failed unit 2 is u; a1 > 0 is a constant parameter of the Erlang distribution; a2(x) is the repair rate of unit 1; b1(x) is the life rate; b2(x) is the repair rate of unit 2; δ(·) is the Dirac-delta function.
Well-posedness of the above model and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until today.

accepted.question_text: For Su's 1997 model of a two-dissimilar-unit system with three modes and random checks, with rates λ1,0, λ2,0, λ0,1, λ0,2 governing partial and total failures, α(x) the check rate, μi,0(x), μ0,i(x), and μi,j(x) the repair-rate functions, and state variables p0,0,k(x,t), p1,0,0(x,t), p0,1,0(x,t), p1,1,0(x,t), p0,1,1(x,t), p1,0,1(x,t), p0,2,0(x,t), p2,0,0(x,t), p1,1,1(x,t), p1,2,0(x,t), and p2,1,0(x,t) describing the possible checked, partially failed, and totally failed system configurations, determine whether the PDE system is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution.

evidence.quote: Where λ1,0 is the failure rate of unit 1 from normal to partial failure; λ2,0 is the failure rate of unit 1 from partial failure to total failure; λ0,1 is the failure rate of unit 2 from normal to partial failure; λ0,2 is the failure rate of unite 2 from partial failure to total failure; α(x) is the check rate satisfying α(x) ≥ 0, ∫_0^∞ α(x)dx = ∞; µi,0(x) (i = 1, 2) is repair rate of of unit 1 satisfying µi,0(x) ≥ 0, ∫_0^∞ µi,0(x)dx = ∞; µ0,i(x) (i = 1, 2) is repair time of unit 2 satisfying µ0,i(x) ≥ 0, ∫_0^∞ µ0,i(x)dx = ∞; µi,j (x) (i, j = 1, 2) is repair rate of both the units satisfying µi,j (x) ≥ 0, ∫_0^∞ µi,j (x)dx = ∞; p0,0,k(x, t) (k ≥ 0) is the probability that unit 1 is normal, unit 2 is normal, the system has been checked k times and has an elapsed time of x; ... p2,1,0(x, t) is the probability that unit 1 is totally failed, unit 2 is partially failed, the system has not been checked and has an elapsed repair time of x..
Well-posedness of the system of the above equations and asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution have not been obtained until now.

accepted.question_text: For the first Yue-Zhu-Qin-Li 2006 model with state variables Q0(x,t), Q1(x,t), Q2(x,t), Q3(x,t), and Q4(x,t), where Q0,Q1,Q2 describe states in which the system is normal and x is the elapsed vacation time of the repairman, Q3 and Q4 describe states in which the system is down and x is the elapsed repair time of the failed piece, λ is the working rate, μ(x) is the repair rate, and α(x) is the repairman's vacation rate, determine whether the PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution in the nonconstant-rate case α(x), μ(x).
accepted.context_brief: First Yue et al. vacation-repairman model

evidence.quote: Here (x, t) ∈ [x, ∞) × [0, ∞); Qi(x, t) (i = 0, 1, 2) is the probability that at time t the system is normal and the elapsed vacation time of repairman is x; Qi(x, t) (i = 3, 4) is the probability that at time t the system is down and the elapsed repair time of the piece is x; λ is the working rate, µ(x) is the repair rate, α(x) is the vacation rate of the repairman, δ(·) is the Dirac-delta function.
When α(x) and µ(x) are non-constants, well-posendess and asymptotic behavior of the time-dependent solutions of the above two models have not been obtained until today.

accepted.question_text: For the second Yue-Zhu-Qin-Li 2006 model with state variables P0(x,t), P1(x,t), P2(x,t), P3(x,t), P4(x,t), P5(x,t), and P6(x,t), where P0,P1,P2,P5 describe states in which the system is normal and x is the elapsed vacation time of the repairman, P3,P4,P6 describe states in which the system is down and x is the elapsed repair time of the failed piece, λ is the working rate, μ(x) is the repair rate, and α(x) is the repairman's vacation rate, determine whether the PDE model is well posed and determine the asymptotic behavior of its time-dependent solution in the nonconstant-rate case α(x), μ(x).
accepted.context_brief: Second Yue et al. vacation-repairman model

evidence.quote: Here (x, t) ∈ [x, ∞)×[0, ∞); Pi(x, t) (i = 0, 1, 2, 5) is the probability that at time t the system is normal and the elapsed vacation time of repairman is x; Pi(x, t) (i = 3, 4, 6) is the probability that at time t the system is down and the elapsed repair time of the piece is x; λ is the working rate, µ(x) is the repair rate, α(x) is the vacation rate of the repairman, δ(·) is the Dirac-delta function.
When α(x) and µ(x) are non-constants, well-posendess and asymptotic behavior of the time-dependent solutions of the above two models have not been obtained until today.
